---
title: Several processes
---

When one process can't get through the data in reasonable time, we split it across the ranks of a `torch.distributed` process group.
Each rank folds its own shard, and the statistics are added.
Since statistics are [monoids](statistics.qmd), the sum is the statistic one process would have computed over all the data.

## With the front door

Each rank calls `lk.laplace` with its own shard, and nothing else changes:

```python
torch.distributed.init_process_group("gloo")  # e.g., under torchrun

# my_shard: this rank's batches, as (inputs, targets) pairs or `lk.Batch` objects
data = lk.data.from_loader(my_shard, n_data=n_total)
post = lk.laplace(model, data, likelihood=lk.Categorical())
```

After each pass, `lk.laplace` combines the statistic with `lk.distributed.all_reduce`.
Every rank then holds the same statistic and builds the same posterior.
Pass `n_data` as the example count over all ranks, not the shard's, since it becomes the posterior's `n_data`.
Every rank needs at least one batch: a rank with none raises, and the others then wait in the collective.

## By hand

`all_reduce(stat)` goes between the last `update` and `finalize`.
With `data` from above, a pass hands out `lk.Batch` objects:

```python
stat = fit.init()

for batch in data(torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)):
    stat = fit.update(stat, batch)

stat = lk.distributed.all_reduce(stat)
curv = fit.finalize(stat)
```

Each rank gathers every rank's statistic and folds them with `+` in rank order.
The rank's own statistic keeps its autograd graph, and the others arrive detached, on the devices of the matching local tensors.
Without a process group, `all_reduce` returns the statistic as it is, so the same code runs on one process.

## What a plugin must do

A plugin needs nothing new here.
`all_reduce` needs a statistic that is a pytree, so that its tensors can be moved to the CPU and back, and that combines with `+`.
It travels with `pickle`, so its class must be importable (see [Immutability and pytrees](pytrees.qmd)).
The statistic doesn't have to be a sum: one with `Requirements(additive_stat=False)` works too.
`lk.testing.check_curvature` checks the monoid law, which is what makes the sum over ranks correct.

::: {.callout-note}
Each batch's generator comes from the fit's seed, the rank's own count of examples before the batch, and the rank itself, so ranks with equal shards draw differently.
A method that draws random numbers, such as a sampled Fisher, therefore draws differently on two ranks than on one process over the same data.
Both are estimates of the same quantity, but their numbers won't match exactly.
:::
